data.cultural_impact: The name Rawat is of Hindu origin and is commonly found in the northern and western parts of India. It is derived from the Sanskrit word "Rawan" which means "to row" or "to move forward." This name was often given to people who were skilled boatmen or who showed great determination and progress in life.

According to the Hindu scriptures, life is a journey, and every individual is a boatman navigating through the ocean of endless opportunities and challenges. Rawat represents a person who is determined to move forward in life, even in the face of adversities, with unwavering faith and courage. The name is also a reminder that every step we take in life brings us closer to our ultimate destination, which is union with the divine.
